title: Black Holes as Licensed Limit Regimes
description: Sets the starting point: a black hole's mass, charge and spin can be described from outside without automatically recovering the individual things that crossed its horizon.
source_sections: Sections 1.3, 4-6, 8-10; formalization boundary in Appendix H

title: Horizon Instability as an Admissible Reconstruction Obstruction
description: Establishes the loss of the exterior connection when no genuine recovery route is available. Saying that information is still stored inside does not restore that connection.
source_sections: Sections 8, 12-15; the finite example follows Definition 14.2 and Theorem 14.4

title: Standingless Interiors and Residual Coherence
description: Explains what happens to matter, energy and spacetime after outside standing is lost: recognisable patterns can remain without their former physical status. Increasing governance-depth means less support for those roles, not a measured distance into the hole.
source_sections: Parts II-IV, especially pages 25-29 and 35-37; main theorem on page 51

title: AMetric Normal-Form Homology
description: Establishes the new AMetric boundary once the full endpoint conditions are met. Its structural conditions match the origin-side boundary, but no matter, energy, information or clock passes through.
source_sections: Section 5, especially Theorem 5.9; Table 6 and Theorem 6.2

title: Black Holes as Constraint-Forced Origins
description: Completes the argument for a fresh interior under the established endpoint conditions. The necessary governance roles recur independently, not by inheritance; the particular contents and history of a populated universe are not specified.
source_sections: Sections 5-7, especially antecedents A1-A9 and Theorem 6.2; target-class hierarchy in Sections 10-12
